<p class="assembly-lede">I thought it would be fun to revisit my introduction to coding, before AI coding assistants, by building a small 8085 simulator around my original 2020 assembly code and logic. Step through the Celsius-to-Fahrenheit conversion and watch the registers and flowchart update.</p>

```{=html}
<section class="assembly-method-grid" aria-label="How the program works">
  <div>
    <h3>1. Divide by five</h3>
    <p>The program repeatedly subtracts five, using register C to count the quotient and the accumulator to retain the remainder.</p>
  </div>
  <div>
    <h3>2. Multiply by nine</h3>
    <p>It repeatedly adds the quotient and uses <code>DAA</code> to keep the intermediate value in binary-coded decimal.</p>
  </div>
  <div>
    <h3>3. Store the result</h3>
    <p>After adding the rounded remainder contribution and 32, it writes the BCD Fahrenheit value to memory address <code>2001h</code>.</p>
  </div>
</section>
```

```{=html}
<section class="assembly-background" aria-labelledby="assembly-background-title">
  <h2 id="assembly-background-title">Project background</h2>
  <p>While earning my associate degree in Electronics Engineering Technology at Wake Technical Community College, I wrote this Intel 8085 assembly program. It was my introduction to programming: working directly with registers, memory addresses, flags and jumps.</p>
  <h3>The assignment</h3>
  <p>Read a Celsius value from memory address <code>2000h</code>, convert any input from 0–37°C into Fahrenheit, store the two-digit binary-coded decimal result at <code>2001h</code>, and document the program with a flowchart and comments.</p>
  <p>The source preserves the instruction sequence and logic I submitted in 2020, including the commented testing harness and the explanations I wrote while learning the material.</p>
  <p>The browser recreation implements the instructions used by this project rather than a complete 8085 emulator. The interactive chart follows the shapes, branches and connections of my October 2020 flowchart, with clarified wording and highlighting linked to the assembly instructions. <a href="assets/8085-assembly/flowchart.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener">View the original PDF</a>.</p>
</section>
```
